hints: Use the common difference property of an arithmetic progression: $u_2 - u_1 = u_3 - u_2$.
Substitute the expressions $u_1 = \frac{p^2}{6}$, $u_2 = 2p - 6$, and $u_3 = p$ into $(2p - 6) - \frac{p^2}{6} = p - (2p - 6)$.
Multiply through by $6$ and rearrange into a quadratic equation $p^2 - 18p + 72 = 0$.
Solve for $p$, then check which value yields all positive terms (or allows a valid sum to infinity in part (b)).
walkthrough:
Set up the common difference relationship for three consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression:
$$u_2 - u_1 = u_3 - u_2 \implies (2p - 6) - \frac{p^2}{6} = p - (2p - 6)$$
$$2p - 6 - \frac{p^2}{6} = 6 - p$$

Rearrange all terms to form a quadratic equation in $p$:
$$3p - 12 - \frac{p^2}{6} = 0 \implies 18p - 72 - p^2 = 0 \implies p^2 - 18p + 72 = 0$$

Factorise the quadratic equation:
$$(p - 6)(p - 12) = 0 \implies p = 6 \quad \text{or} \quad p = 12$$

For $p = 6$, the terms are $6, 6, 6$ (a constant sequence with common difference $0$), whereas for $p = 12$, the terms are $24, 18, 12$ (all strictly positive with common difference $d = -6$). To allow a convergent GP in part (b), we select:
$$p = 12$$

hints: Substitute $p = 12$ to find the first two terms of the GP: $a = \frac{12^2}{6} = 24$ and $u_2 = 2(12) - 6 = 18$.
Use the sum to infinity formula $S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - r}$ since $|r| < 1$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the first two terms of the geometric progression using $p = 12$:
$$a = \frac{p^2}{6} = \frac{12^2}{6} = \frac{144}{6} = 24$$
$$u_2 = 2p - 6 = 2(12) - 6 = 18$$

Compute the sum to infinity using $S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - r}$ (since $|r| = \frac{3}{4} < 1$):
$$S_\infty = \frac{24}{1 - \frac{3}{4}} = \frac{24}{\frac{1}{4}} = 96$$
